entities.name: Virtual International Authority File
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary:
The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF) is a monumental collaborative international authority file service, initiated around 2003, that aggregates and links the authority records of national libraries and other cultural institutions worldwide. It directly addresses the historical challenge of disambiguating names of persons, corporate bodies, and works across different cataloging systems and languages, thereby revolutionizing bibliographic control and research discoverability on a global scale. Key players in its inception and ongoing development include the Online Computer Library Center (OCLC), the Library of Congress (LoC), and the German National Library (DNB), alongside dozens of other national bibliographic agencies.

Developed as a joint pilot project by OCLC, the Library of Congress, and the German National Library in the early 2000s, VIAF moved from its initial experimental phase in 2003 to a fully operational service by 2007. It employs sophisticated algorithms to cluster authority records for the same entity from contributing institutions, assigning a unique VIAF identifier to each cluster. By 2012, it had incorporated data from over 30 national and regional libraries, including the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the National Library of Israel, expanding its scope to encompass millions of authority records and establishing itself as a critical global infrastructure for information science.
